title: Move into product inside your company
summary: For many people the easiest route into product is inside the organisation they already know. Build a case for a real problem, take on product work and ask for the role.

beginner: Find product managers in your organisation and learn how people there moved into the role. Ask your manager and HR which routes exist, such as secondments, associate roles or shadowing.
Choose a real problem in your own area and write a one-page business case: the problem, the evidence, a proposed change and its value.
Tell your manager you are aiming for product, share the business case and ask what would make them support the move.
Ask to shadow a PM for a few days, to join a team's discovery session or to take on PM-like work in your current job, such as owning a measure, running user interviews or writing a brief.
Keep a log of outcomes you owned, decisions you made and what happened, using the language of the PM skills framework.
Look at internal vacancies and talk to the hiring manager before you apply.
If the answer is 'not yet', ask what to work on and agree a date to review it.

toolExamples.notion: Keep a log with the date, what you owned, what you decided and what happened.

definitionOfDone: Conversations held with your manager and with a PM
A log of PM-like work with outcomes
pitfalls: Dropping your current responsibilities before the move is agreed
Asking for the title before showing the work
